F-138_substrate.title: NUMBERING COLLISION — substrate self-filed F-138 (execution writes missing) conflicts with auditor's F-138 (ias-executor-ts)
F-138_substrate.details: dev-response-009 (filed 2026-05-27T11:35Z) used the designation 'F-138 (NEW, MEDIUM)' for a separate finding: freshly-seeded template execution writes not landing in trace tables. The substrate closed the auditor's F-138 in iter 17 and treats the two as distinct findings. However, the shared label creates permanent ambiguity in the audit record.
F-138_substrate.collision_pattern: This is at least the 3rd occurrence of the substrate filing findings under auditor-reserved F-numbers. Prior collisions: F-129 (partially), F-130. The substrate does not have an independent finding numbering namespace, and F-numbers are assigned sequentially by the auditor. Each collision creates a record that appears to reference a single issue but addresses two.
F-138_substrate.recommendation: Substrate-originated findings should use a distinct prefix (e.g., 'S-' or 'DEV-') rather than the 'F-' namespace reserved for auditor findings. This is a LOW process risk but accumulates into audit record integrity issues over time.
F-138_substrate.auditor_verdict: DOCUMENTED — recommend namespace separation in next operational iteration

process_findings.title: ias-executor-ts lacks GitHub remote — network-unreachable on fresh clone
process_findings.details: The F-138 mitigation (bundle + gitlink advance) preserves the 3 untracked commits within the repository tree, but ias-executor-ts has no .gitmodules entry and no GitHub remote. A fresh git clone of the super-repo + git submodule update --init would fail to reconstruct ias-executor-ts from any network source. The bundle in validation/recovery/ is a local-only mitigation.
process_findings.recommendation: Operator should create the GitHub remote and add a .gitmodules entry. Until then, any new developer environment must manually restore from the bundle.
